title_en: Python I: from value to function, collections, files and environments (part 1 of 2)
how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

storyboard_notes.text: This dive pre-empts CH-07 (first taught here: c:bug, c:containers, c:dictionary, c:list, c:set, c:tuple). Close the dive with a forward callback card '-> CH-07'; CH-07 opens with a match-cut callback to this dive's visual (04 section 11: call back to earlier scenes).

sentences.ar: أهلا بكم في شرحنا الجديد
sentences.en: Welcome to our new explainer.

sentences.ar: هدفنا النهاردة مش مجرد أننا نحفظ شوية كود أو syntax tricks
sentences.en: Today's goal isn't just memorizing some code or syntax tricks.

sentences.ar: إحنا هنا عشان نبني Mental Model أو نموذج ذهني حقيقي لطريقة شغل لغة Python من جوة
sentences.en: We're here to build a real mental model of how Python works from the inside.

sentences.ar: هنشوف إزاي الكود بيتنفس خطوة بخطوة
sentences.en: We'll see how code breathes, step by step.

sentences.ar: وهنعتمد بشكل أساسي على تقنية الـcode trace
sentences.en: We'll rely mainly on the code-trace technique.

sentences.ar: يعني السطر هيكون منور وجنبه لوحة أسماء بأسهم بتشاور على القيم وstack frames بتطلع وتنزل قدامنا
sentences.en: The current line is lit, next to it a names panel with arrows pointing to values, and stack frames rising and falling in front of us.

sentences.ar: الأجندة بتاعتنا سريعة ومكثفة
sentences.en: Our agenda is quick and dense.

sentences.ar: هنبدأ بأساسيات الذاكرة والتحكم وبعدين الحلقات والدوال وهياكل البيانات وتكلفتها وهنعدي على كروت المقابلات المهمة جداً وفي الآخر هنختم بحفظ البيانات والبيئات الإفتراضية
sentences.en: We start with memory and control basics, then loops and functions, data structures and their cost, key interview cards, and finally saving data and virtual environments.

sentences.ar: أساسيات الذاكرة وإزاي مسار التحكم بيشتغل بجد
sentences.en: Memory basics, and how control flow really works.

sentences.ar: في لغات برمجة تانية ممكن نتخيل المتغير كأنه صندوق بنحط فيه قيمة
sentences.en: In other programming languages we might picture a variable as a box we put a value into.

sentences.ar: في الـcode trace اللي قدامنا شايفين السطر المنور؟
sentences.en: In the code trace in front of us, see the highlighted line?

sentences.ar: الاسم price مربوط بسهم للقيمة 100 والاسم qty مربوط بسهم للقيمة 3
sentences.en: The name price is bound by an arrow to the value 100, and the name qty by an arrow to the value 3.

sentences.ar: ولما نيجي نحسب الـtotal بيتخلق سهم جديد بيشاور على القيمة 300
sentences.en: When we compute total, a new arrow is created pointing to the value 300.

sentences.ar: السهم ده معناه هوية أو identity
sentences.en: That arrow means identity.

sentences.ar: وبما إن كل قيمة لها نوع زي الأرقام أو النصوص فمهم جدا نعمل validation أو تدقيق لمدخلات المستخدم
sentences.en: Since every value has a type, like numbers or text, it's very important to validate user input.

sentences.ar: عشان لو حد كتب كلمة بدل الرقم الدنيا هتبوظ مننا لو مش عاملين حسابنا
sentences.en: Because if someone types a word instead of the number, things break on us if we haven't planned for it.

sentences.ar: مثلاً لو بنصنف عملاء الـVIP دفعوا أكبر من أو يساوي 10,000 والـGold 5,000 والـSilver 1,000
sentences.en: For example, classifying customers: VIPs paid 10,000 or more, Gold 5,000, and Silver 1,000.

sentences.ar: المؤشر بيمشي في الفرع اللي شرطه بيتحقق الأول
sentences.en: The pointer takes the first branch whose condition is true.

sentences.ar: عشان كده الترتيب هنا مصيري
sentences.en: That's why the order here is decisive.

sentences.ar: لو حطينا شرط الألف في الأول المؤشر هيدخل فيه فوراً وكل عملاء الـVIP هيتصنفوا بالغلط كـSilver
sentences.en: If we put the 1,000 condition first, the pointer enters it immediately and all VIP customers get wrongly classified as Silver.

sentences.ar: القسم التاني بياخدنا الخطوة أعمق الحلقات والمجمعات وازاي الدوال بتتنفس في الذاكرة
sentences.en: Section two takes us a step deeper: loops, accumulators, and how functions breathe in memory.

sentences.ar: ودلوقتي جه وقت أول سؤال توقع علينا ركزوا معايا
sentences.en: Now it's time for our first prediction question; focus with me.

sentences.ar: عندنا لوب بتلف على خمس طلبات وفي مجمع أو accumulator اسمه total بيجمع الطلبات اللي توصلت بس واللي هم تلت طلبات
sentences.en: We have a loop running over five orders, and an accumulator named total that sums only the delivered orders, which are three.

sentences.ar: يا ترى قبل اللفة الأخيرة من اللوب مباشرة قيمة الـtotal هتبقى كام؟
sentences.en: Right before the loop's last iteration, what will total be?

sentences.ar: فكروا فيها ثواني قبل ما نقلب السلايد
sentences.en: Think about it for a few seconds before we flip the slide.

sentences.ar: لو الإجابة اللي جات في بالكم هي 2 أو 3 فده معناه إن الكود بتاعكم سليم وممتاز
sentences.en: If the answer that came to your mind is 2 or 3, that means your code is sound and excellent.

sentences.ar: لكن لو الإجابة صفر فده بيكشف عن bug شهير جداً بنقع فيه
sentences.en: But if the answer is zero, that reveals a very famous bug we fall into.

sentences.ar: النتيجة إن القيمة قبل اللفة الأخيرة هتبقى صفر والنتيجة النهائية هتبقى حالة آخر طلب بس
sentences.en: So the value before the last iteration will be zero, and the final result will be just the last order's state.

sentences.ar: من اللوبس نروح للـfunctions
sentences.en: From loops we move on to functions.

sentences.ar: يعني لو بنحسب سعر بخصمة 15% القيمة بتتربط بـ85
sentences.en: For instance, if we compute a price with a 15% discount, the value gets bound to 85.

sentences.ar: الشغل كله بيحصل جوه الإطار ده
sentences.en: All the work happens inside this frame.

sentences.ar: وملحوظة سريعة، لو ما عملناش return واضحة الـfunction بترجع None تلقائياً
sentences.en: Quick note: if we don't write an explicit return, the function returns None automatically.

sentences.ar: ولما بنكتب اسم متغير، الـPython بتدور عليه إزاي؟
sentences.en: When we write a variable name, how does Python look it up?

sentences.ar: بتمشي على قاعدة اسمها LEGB الدوائر المتداخلة دي بتشرحها ببساطة
sentences.en: It follows a rule called LEGB, which these nested circles explain simply.

sentences.ar: بتبدأ تدور محلياً local جوه الـfunction
sentences.en: It starts by searching locally, inside the function.

sentences.ar: لو ما لقتوش، بتوسع الدايرة للنطاق المحيط وبعدين النطاق العام في الملف كله وأخيراً الأسماء المدمجة في اللغة نفسها
sentences.en: If it doesn't find it, it widens the circle to the enclosing scope, then the global scope across the whole file, and finally the names built into the language itself.

sentences.ar: النظام ده بيمنع أي لخبطة في التسميات
sentences.en: This system prevents any naming confusion.

sentences.ar: هندخل دلوقتي على القسم الثالث هياكل البيانات وإزاي نختار الحاوية المناسبة من غير ما ندفع تكلفة عالية في الأداء
sentences.en: Now into section three: data structures, and how to pick the right container without paying a high performance cost.

sentences.ar: الأربع حاويات اللي قدامنا دول هم الأساس
sentences.en: These four containers in front of us are the foundation.

sentences.ar: الـlist عبارة عن صف مترتب نقدر نعدل فيه ونكرر البيانات وبنوصل لأي عنصر بالـindex
sentences.en: A list is an ordered row: we can modify it, repeat data, and reach any element by index.

sentences.ar: الـtuple زيه بالظبط بس مقفول وما ينفعش يتعدل وده بيخليه ممتاز كمفتاح في قاموس
sentences.en: A tuple is just like it but locked and unchangeable, which makes it great as a key in a dictionary.

sentences.ar: الـset بقى عبارة عن كيس ما بيهتمش بترتيب خالص بس الميزة الجبارة بتاعته انه بيمنع التكرار تماما
sentences.en: A set is a bag that doesn't care about order at all, but its great feature is that it completely prevents duplicates.

sentences.ar: وأخيرا القاموس أو الـdictionary بيربط key بـvalue ومن أول إصدار Python 3.7 بقى بيحفظ على ترتيب الإدخال
sentences.en: And finally the dictionary maps a key to a value, and since Python 3.7 it preserves insertion order.

sentences.ar: وهنا نوصل لسؤال التوقع التاني
sentences.en: And here we reach the second prediction question.

sentences.ar: لو عايزين نعمل فحص وجود أو membership test عشان نشوف عنصر معين موجود في مجموعة بيانات فيها عشر تلاف عنصر ولا لأ
sentences.en: If we want to do an existence check, a membership test, to see whether an element is in a dataset of ten thousand elements or not...

sentences.ar: تفتكروا مين فيهم هيخلص الفحص أسرع الـlist ولا الـset
sentences.en: Which one do you think finishes the check faster, the list or the set?

sentences.ar: الإجابة واضحة جداً في الـsplit screen اللي قدامنا
sentences.en: The answer is very clear in the split screen in front of us.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: A readable, general-purpose programming language widely used for data analysis, automatio…
concepts.failure: Using plain loops over huge data instead of vectorized pandas or SQL operations.

concepts.def_en: Last-in, first-out structure; in memory, the call stack where function frames are pushed…
concepts.failure: Mixing up stack and heap, or recursing too deeply until the stack overflows.

concepts.def_en: The order in which statements run, steered by if/else branches, loops and function calls,…
concepts.failure: Assuming every branch runs; in an if/elif chain only the first match does.

concepts.def_en: A name bound to a value in memory that your code can read and change; in Python, a label…
concepts.failure: Picturing a variable as a box, so shared references surprise you.

concepts.def_en: A path the program can take at a decision point, chosen by a condition such as if/else; i…
concepts.failure: Leaving one branch untested, so bugs hide on the path rarely taken.

concepts.def_en: A construct that repeats a block of code for each item or until a condition changes.
concepts.failure: Off-by-one bounds, or a condition that never changes, looping forever.

concepts.def_en: A variable that collects a running result across loop iterations, such as a total or list…
concepts.failure: Initialising it inside the loop, so it resets every iteration.

concepts.def_en: A named, reusable block of code that takes inputs, does a calculation and returns a value.
concepts.failure: Forgetting return, so the function silently gives back None.

concepts.def_en: A defect in code or configuration that makes a program behave differently from what was intended.
concepts.def_ar: عيب في الكود أو الإعدادات بيخلّي البرنامج يتصرف بشكل مختلف عن المقصود.
concepts.failure: Fixing symptoms without finding the root cause or adding a test, so the bug returns.

concepts.def_en: An ordered, changeable Python collection that allows duplicates and index access; checking membership means scanning every element.
concepts.def_ar: collection مرتّبة وقابلة للتعديل في Python بتسمح بالتكرار والوصول بالـindex؛ والبحث فيها معناه المرور على كل العناصر.
concepts.failure: Using list membership checks on large data, where a set or dict is far faster.

concepts.def_en: A separate sorted lookup structure on one or more columns that lets a database find rows…
concepts.failure: Adding an index on every column; each one slows writes and may never be used.

concepts.def_en: A fixed, ordered Python record that cannot change after creation, so it can serve as a dictionary key.
concepts.def_ar: سجل ثابت ومرتّب في Python مينفعش يتعدّل بعد ما يتعمل، عشان كده ينفع يبقى key في dict.
concepts.failure: Forgetting the trailing comma, so a one-element tuple is just the bare value.

concepts.def_en: A Python collection mapping unique keys to values, giving near-instant O(1) lookup by key.
concepts.def_ar: collection في Python بتربط كل key فريد بـvalue، وبتدّي lookup سريع جدًا O(1) بالـkey.
concepts.failure: Indexing a missing key directly and getting KeyError instead of using get.

concepts.def_en: An unordered Python collection that guarantees each element appears once and checks membership fast.
concepts.def_ar: collection في Python من غير ترتيب، وبتضمن إن كل عنصر يظهر مرة واحدة بس، والبحث فيها سريع.
concepts.failure: Expecting a set to keep insertion order or allow indexing like a list.

concepts.def_en: An automated check that runs code and asserts the expected result, so changes that break behaviour are caught early.
concepts.def_ar: الـtest فحص آلي بيشغّل الكود ويتأكد إن النتيجة زي المتوقع، عشان أي تغيير يكسر السلوك يتكشف بدري.
concepts.failure: Tests that never fail prove nothing; first watch the test fail, then fix.

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.

A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.

An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
A collection morphing between types (list -> set -> dict ...).
Virtual environments as domes isolating package sets.
Commits on branches; checkout, commit and merge on anchors.
Tests that run and pass, fail or skip before a merge gate.
